chapter_title: The Interpretation of Happiness, Wisdom and Power;
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Three Divine Attributes as Received in Every Plane of the Mind

---

**¶2:** [GAP-1: REVIEW — the inquiry concerns] the three essential realities that in the external mind are called "blessedness," "illumination," and "efficacy" — the three attributes by which the Divine is received.

---

**¶5:** The blessedness of the Divine Glory is the Divine Good itself, the God of [GAP-2: REVIEW — divine truth, who] is established in the inmost state of [GAP-3: REVIEW — wisdom]. His glorious illumination is the Great Proceeding Divine Truth that [GAP-4: — descends and flows forth] into the lower degrees, which flows through all states of spiritual life, and those states are sustained within it. His great efficacy is the totality of divine faculties, abundant goods, and ministering truths that were called forth from Him as they [GAP-5: — went forth and constituted] what are called the successive states of the spiritual world [GAP-6: — in their order and fullness].

---

**¶6:** [GAP-7: — There is also the containing form of celestial good] which is called the inmost love [GAP-8: — the containing form of] divine love in act, [GAP-9: — wherein dwells the mediating principle of divine love], the second degree of eminence [GAP-10: — in the celestial kingdom]. The glorious [GAP-11: REVIEW — blessedness] is the [GAP-12: REVIEW — Active] Divine Proceeding, [GAP-13: — the origin of all spiritual life; and the illumination] is the Matrix of Divine Truth from which all life proceeds [GAP-14: — in its generative fullness; and the great efficacy] is [GAP-15: REVIEW — the totality of] divine faculties, [GAP-16: REVIEW — the] abundant goods and the ministering truths that dwell within this containing form of love.

---

**¶7:** Again, blessedness, illumination, and efficacy exist within the containing form of divine truth [GAP-17: — in its own distinct order]. The blessedness [GAP-18: — that dwells therein is] the Inmost Intention of the Divine Good. Also, the illumination is the Pure Uncorrupted Wisdom of the Divine. And the efficacy that is within this vessel of truth is [GAP-19: REVIEW — the totality of] divine faculties, the abundant goods, and the ministering truths that are established within it.

---

**¶8:** Again, these three exist within the fundamental constituents of the regenerate life: blessedness, illumination, and efficacy. The blessedness is [GAP-20: REVIEW — the Sustaining Principle of Divine Good in Act], the fully regenerate human form. The illumination is the [GAP-21: REVIEW — five derivative truths proceeding from the] Active Divine Proceeding; and the great efficac[GAP-22: y is — the] five derivative goods from the primordial celestial state [GAP-23: — which are interiorly present] and compounded throughout the whole of the spiritual organism, so that [GAP-24: — they pervade every state] while the sustaining principle upholds the whole.

---

## Translator's Note

The chapter teaches that three divine attributes — blessedness (the reception of Good), illumination (the reception of Truth), and efficacy (their conjunction in act) — are present on every successive plane of the mind: in the inmost celestial degree (¶5, the containing form of love), in the spiritual degree (¶6–7, containing forms of love and truth respectively as distinct vessels), and in the natural degree where the constitutive elements of regenerate life are formed (¶8). The "ships" are containing forms — vessels in the Swedenborgian sense — through which divine influx is received at each level. The "five sons" in ¶8 correspond to the five derivative truths and goods that constitute the sensory and natural planes of the mind, enclosed within the whole and sustaining it from within.

fills.explanation: The standard interrogative opening for a Kephalaia question chapter; the inquiry asks what the three things are — confirmed by the spiritual reading's "the inquiry concerns."
"The God of truth" is the standard Manichaean/Kephalaia title for the Father of Greatness, and "who" introduces the relative clause describing his establishment in the land of light.
"The great land of light" is the fixed Manichaean term for the divine realm where the Father is established; it corresponds to the inmost state of wisdom/love in the spiritual reading.

The Great Spirit (divine truth) extends from the heights downward through all aeons; "reaches from above to below" expresses the descent described in the spiritual reading as "descends and flows forth into the lower degrees."

The spiritual reading says the divine faculties "went forth and constituted" the aeons; the gods and angels were summoned as they came forth, and they ARE those called aeons — a standard Coptic resumptive identification clause.

"Aeons of the greatness" is a fixed Kephalaia phrase designating the divine realms; the spiritual reading's "successive states of the spiritual world in their order and fullness" is precisely what "aeons of the greatness" denotes in the natural register.

fills.fill: Again, these three exist in that
fills.explanation: Parallels ¶7's opening "Again, happiness, wisdom and power exist in the ship of living waters"; ¶6 introduces the same three attributes within the sun-ship, using "that which is called the sun" as a relative construction.

The sun is identified as the ship of living fire; "it is the ship of" provides the equative clause linking "that which is called the sun" to its Manichaean designation as the containing vessel of living fire.

fills.fill: in which dwells the Third Amba
fills.explanation: The Third Ambassador is the presiding deity of the sun-ship in Manichaean cosmology; the spiritual reading confirms "wherein dwells the mediating principle of divine love," and the legible "ssador" completes "Ambassador."

Completes "greatness" and identifies the Third Ambassador as "the second greatness of the ship," then transitions with "The" to the listing of happiness, wisdom, and power; the spiritual reading says "in the celestial kingdom" = "of the ship."

The chapter consistently uses "happiness" as one of the three attributes (happiness, wisdom, power); confirmed by the spiritual reading's "blessedness" which corresponds to "happiness" in the Kephalaia's natural register.

The "Living Spirit" is the standard Manichaean divine figure who corresponds to the active divine proceeding; confirmed by the spiritual reading's "Active Divine Proceeding" which maps to "Living Spirit" in Kephalaia vocabulary.

fills.fill: the first greatness; and the wisdom
fills.explanation: Since the Third Ambassador is called "the second greatness," the Living Spirit is naturally "the first greatness" in the ship's hierarchy; the transition to "the wisdom is the Mother of Life" follows the chapter's triadic pattern.
Completes "Life" and transitions to the third attribute; parallels ¶5's "His great power is all the gods" and ¶7's "And the power that is in the ship is all the gods" — a simple structural bridge.

"All the gods" is the consistent formula throughout the chapter for the power attribute, representing the totality of divine faculties at each level; confirmed by the spiritual reading's "the totality of."
The definite article before "rich ones" is required by the fixed Kephalaia formula "all the gods, the rich ones and the angels" used consistently in ¶5, ¶6, and ¶7.

Parallel to ¶6 where the sun ship is identified by name ("which is called the sun"); the ship of living waters is the moon in Manichaean cosmology, and naming it here follows the chapter's structural pattern.

The spiritual reading says "that dwells therein is"; in the Kephalaia's register "in it is" naturally locates the happiness within the ship of living waters, reading "the happiness in it is the Mind of the Father."
Confirms the same fixed formula "all the gods, the rich ones and the angels" used at every level of the chapter for the power attribute.

The Pillar of Glory (Column of Glory / Stelê tês Doxês) is the standard Manichaean figure equated with the Perfect Man in the Kephalaia; it corresponds to the spiritual reading's "Sustaining Principle of Divine Good in Act."

The "five sons of the Living Spirit" are the five cosmic rulers (Holder, King of Honour, Adamas, King of Glory, Atlas) — a fixed Manichaean category representing derivative truths from the Active Divine Proceeding.

Completes "power" and directly identifies the great power as "the five sons of the First Man" (the five light elements); the spiritual reading confirms a direct equation with the dash "y is — the," indicating no intervening text.

fills.explanation: The five sons of the First Man, all of them, are enclosed and compounded in the totality — a resumptive "all of them" emphasizes their completeness within the mixture, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "which are interiorly present."
